title: How to Change Default Search Engine in Firefox - Bing, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia
description: How to change the default search engine in Firefox?  In this tutorial, I show you how to change your default search engine in the Firefox browser.  This is great if you are looking to switch to Bing, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, etc and will update the search engine for anything you search within the search bar or address bar.  More Firefox tutorials: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL8griS8Ww-KlP3Gc6SEmaXhuiIZMYqEsK More Internet Tutorials: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL8griS8Ww-KlLAJuyfDamNc-V6uUMOHk3  How to change your default search engine in Firefox: 1. Select the Menu by selecting the three horizontal lines in the top right corner.  2. Select Options. 3. Once the options load, select Search in the left side bar. 4. Under Default Search Engine, you should see your current default search engine (in this example it is Bing).  If you select the drop-down box, you will see a list of pre-configured search engines.   5. If your desired search engine isn't in the list of available search engines,, scroll down to One-Click Search Engines and select Find More Search Engines at the bottom. 6. In the top-left corner, you can search for the search engine of your choice.  If you do this, make sure the Add-on Type is set to Search Tool. 7. Once you have found your desired search engine (in this example I’m using Ecosia), select it and then Select + Add to Firefox.  When the pop-up appears, select Add. 8. Return to the Firefox options and select your newly added search engine in the drop-down menu under Default Search Engine.  This will automatically save your new default search engine. 9. Test this to be sure that it worked properly by searching for something to see if it opens in the correct search engine.  #Firefox #DuckDuckGo #SearchEngine  Disclaimer: Some of the links in this description are Amazon affiliate links. asr.full_text: Hey guys, welcome to another Gaging Gadgets Firefox tutorial video. In this video I'm going to show you how you can change the default search engine for your Firefox browser. So when I say default search engine what I mean is the search engine used when you search for anything in the search bar, or in the address bar. So let's go ahead and get started. The first thing we need to do to change the default search engine in Firefox is simply open the menu by selecting the 3 horizontal lines in the top right. Then once the menu opens, go down to Options. Select that, and then in the options, we'll go to the left side bar and we'll select Search. So as you can see here, we have an area called Default Search Engine. This is where you can select some pre-configured search engines. You could change it to Google, DuckDuckGo if you're into privacy, also different web sites as well. If your desired search engine is not in this list, all you need to do is scroll down until you see one-click search engines and then go to find more search engines at the bottom. Select that. As you can see here, Firefox has almost 4,000 search engines available for you to select. So all you need to do is go through this list here, find your desired search engine. You can also use the search bar right here to search for specific search engines. All you need to do is make sure that the add-on type is search tools. So I'm gonna add Ecosia, which is a search engine that plants trees every time you use the search engine, so I'm going to select the search plug-in and then just select Add to Firefox, and then OK. Once it's installed all we need to do is go back to the Firefox options, and then in the drop down we'll find our new desired search engine and we can select it. Once you select the search engine, you're done. You don't have to save anything, it automatically saves, and when I do a search, it'll be at my new desired search engine. So that's how you change the default search engine in Firefox. If you have any questions about this, leave a comment below, and I'll get back to you as soon as I can. If you'd like to see more Firefox Tutorials, check the links in the description. If this video helped you, give it a thumbs up, and please consider subscribing to my channel, Gaging Gadgets, for more gadget reviews and tech tutorials. Thank you so much for watching.
